raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

#47512 made the JIT softmax the first choice on the SM100 family, but three pieces of text still say that Cake does this work: a comment in `test_softmax.py`, the Cake README, and the name of a CPU test. On a B200, these statements are false. Serving is not affected, but the text can mislead a person who debugs SM100 sampling.

## Modifications

This PR changes text only. The comment now names the JIT softmax. The test name now says fallback, because the JIT softmax is not selected on a CPU runner. The README now says that Cake runs in `sampling.softmax` only when the JIT softmax rejects a call in the Cake domain, and that DSpark's draft softmax still reaches Cake through FlashInfer.

Temporary counters, not in this PR, show where Cake still runs on B200 with FlashInfer 0.7.2:

| Run | `sampling.softmax` | FlashInfer Cake softmax |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_softmax.py` | JIT for eligible shapes, otherwise Torch | Not called |
| Llama-3.2-1B, TP 1 and TP 2, sampled requests | JIT | Not called |
| Llama-3.1-8B with EAGLE3, sampled requests | JIT | Not called |
| Qwen3-14B with `dspark_qwen3_14b_block7`, sampled requests | JIT | Called with shapes such as `(28, 151936)` |
| Same DSpark server, greedy requests | Not called | Not called |

Llama's vocabulary (128256) is inside the `supports_softmax` domain, so the JIT softmax takes inputs that Cake also accepts. The DSpark server used the flags and environment of `test_basic_sanity_dspark.py`. `SoftmaxTemp` is the only serving caller of FlashInfer's softmax outside the Cake adapter.

The Cake branch of `sampling.softmax` ran only for tensors that I built by hand, such as `x[:, :V]` from a tensor of width `V + 1`, with temperatures. A code read found no serving caller that passes such a tensor, but it was not a full audit.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable, because this PR changes no runtime code. On a trial merge with main at `b6a59c4938`, these checks are clean: `test_softmax.py` on a B200, `test_kernels_namespace.py` on a CPU-only lease, and pre-commit on the changed files.

Nothing ran on SM103, GB200, or GB300. The SM103 statements come from reading `_device_supported` and FlashInfer's `_supports_blackwell_softmax`. I read the DSpark shard and blockwise-rejection branches but did not run them.

The Cake tests that call `sampling.softmax` fail on a B200 host with `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'stride'`, because the JIT softmax is selected there. CI runs them on CPU runners only, so it does not see this existing failure.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -10,13 +10,19 @@ and numerical contract. In particular, Cake top-k-then-top-p sampling is not a
 drop-in replacement for joint top-k/top-p filtering. Prepared plans must remain
 valid when input contents and buffers change across calls and CUDA Graph replay.
 
-The sampler's softmax fast path accepts FP32 contiguous logits on SM100 and
-SM103, small batches and large vocabularies. The sampler retains its existing
-filtering and random-number generation, and deterministic inference retains
-torch.softmax.
+In `sampling.softmax`, SM100-family GPUs run the JIT softmax first. The Cake
+softmax runs only when the JIT softmax rejects the call and the logits, after
+any temperature scaling, are FP32 and contiguous on SM100 or SM103, with a small
+batch and a large vocabulary. The sampler retains its existing filtering and
+random-number generation, and deterministic inference retains torch.softmax.
 Other operators require their own numerical and real-model performance evidence
 before being added here.
 
-The fast path also requires FlashInfer's `cake_blackwell_softmax` module. Older
-FlashInfer installations retain Torch softmax; this adapter does not change
-SGLang's dependency pins.
+The Cake softmax in `sampling.softmax` also requires FlashInfer's
+`cake_blackwell_softmax` module. With an older FlashInfer, that path uses Torch
+softmax. This adapter does not change SGLang's dependency pins.
+
+DSpark's `SoftmaxTemp` (in `ops/speculative/dspark/dspark_accept.py`) calls
+FlashInfer's softmax directly and does not use this adapter. It computes the
+draft softmax, and the target softmax for requests with no top-k or top-p.
+FlashInfer routes that call to its Cake softmax on SM100 and SM103.

+# SM100 runs exercise the JIT softmax path for eligible shapes.
 register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
 # backend-specific: ROCm uses the temperature_softmax kernel for per-row scaling.
 register_amd_ci(est_time=10, stage="stage-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small-amd")
